title: Recurring Monthly Donations: A Setup Guide for SEA Nonprofits
summary: Learn how nonprofits in Singapore, Malaysia, and the Philippines can set up recurring monthly donations — with the right tools, compliance steps, and payment methods.
body_markdown:
**Quick Answer:** Nonprofits in Singapore, Malaysia, and the Philippines can collect recurring monthly donations by combining a compliant payment platform with local payment methods — PayNow (SG), DuitNow QR (MY), and GCash or ShopeePay recurring (PH). HitPay, licensed by the[Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS)](https://www.mas.gov.sg/) , supports recurring billing and donation links across all three markets with no monthly platform fees and next business day payouts for domestic transactions.


Donor retention is the core funding challenge for most nonprofits in Southeast Asia. One-time campaigns generate short bursts of revenue; recurring monthly giving creates the stable, forecastable cash flow that allows organisations to plan programmes, hire staff, and commit to multi-year impact. Yet many charities in the region still rely on manual bank transfers or annual pledge drives — friction-heavy processes that erode donor commitment over time.


The shift toward digital payment infrastructure changes this equation. According to[Google-Temasek e-Conomy SEA](https://economysea.withgoogle.com/) , digital payment volumes across Southeast Asia continue to grow rapidly, and donor expectations are following the same trajectory. Supporters now expect to set up a recurring contribution in under two minutes — the same experience they get with a streaming subscription.


This guide explains how nonprofits across Singapore, Malaysia, and the Philippines can build a recurring donation system that works.


## What regulatory requirements apply to charities accepting digital donations?


Charities and religious organisations are classified as restricted businesses under most payment platform acceptable use policies — meaning they require additional documentation before an account can be fully activated for transactions. This is standard across the industry, not a barrier unique to any single provider.


In Singapore, charities registered with the Commissioner of Charities must comply with the Charities Act and relevant MAS guidelines on payment services. In Malaysia, organisations should be registered with the Registrar of Societies (ROS) or Companies Commission of Malaysia (SSM) and comply with Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) guidelines. In the Philippines, nonprofits are registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and must observe Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) regulations for digital payment acceptance.


When applying to a payment platform, charities should prepare:


1.


Certificate of registration or incorporation


2.


Constitution or memorandum and articles of association


3.


Latest audited financial statements


4.


Details of authorised signatories and beneficial owners


5.


Description of fundraising activities and intended use of funds


Approval timelines vary by platform and the completeness of documentation submitted.


## What payment methods should nonprofits offer donors in each market?


Donor completion rates drop significantly when a preferred payment method is absent. Nonprofits operating across Singapore, Malaysia, and the Philippines need to match local payment behaviour — not force donors onto international card flows.


Market


Recommended Methods for Recurring Donations


Singapore 🇸🇬


PayNow, Visa/Mastercard, GrabPay


Malaysia 🇲🇾


DuitNow, Touch 'n Go, GrabPay, Visa/Mastercard


Philippines 🇵🇭


GCash, ShopeePay (recurring); Maya, QR Ph, cards (one-off links)


Card-on-file is the most reliable method for automated recurring charges — the donor's card is stored securely (PCI DSS compliance required) and charged on a set cycle without any action from the donor. Wallet-based recurring is now available: on HitPay, GCash recurring payments let donors in the Philippines authorise once, for Philippine-registered organisations and for organisations outside the Philippines.


For donors who prefer bank transfers, payment links sent monthly via WhatsApp or email remain a practical fallback — though they require donor action each cycle and therefore carry higher drop-off risk than card-on-file.


Understanding[the differences between digital wallets and payment gateways](https://hitpayapp.com/blog/digital-wallet-vs-payment-gateways) helps nonprofits decide which combination of payment rails best fits their donor demographics.


## How do nonprofits set up recurring donation links in practice?


The most practical approach for most small-to-mid-size charities is a no-code recurring payment link — a shareable URL that prompts a donor to enter card or wallet details once, then triggers automatic charges on a monthly cycle.


HitPay's recurring billing feature enables nonprofits to create donation links with fixed or donor-selected amounts, set monthly billing cycles, and receive automatic payouts. The setup process is:


1.


Register for a HitPay account and submit charity documentation for review


2.


Once approved, navigate to **Payment Links > Recurring Billing** in the dashboard


3.


Set the donation amount (fixed or open) and billing frequency (monthly)


4.


Customise the link with the organisation's name and campaign description


5.


Share the link via email, WhatsApp, social media, or embed it on a website


6.


Donors enter card details once — all subsequent charges are automatic


Payouts from domestic transactions settle the next business day in SGD (Singapore), MYR (Malaysia), and PHP (Philippines). Cross-border donations settle at T+2.


For a broader look at how recurring billing works across different business models,[the guide to automating subscription payments with HitPay's recurring billing](https://hitpayapp.com/blog/how-to-use-recurring-billing) covers the technical setup in detail.


## How should nonprofits handle donor communication and failed payments?


Recurring giving programmes fail not at sign-up, but at churn — donors who forget why they gave, or whose cards expire without a replacement being captured.


Best practices for retention:


-


Send a confirmation email immediately after the first successful charge, including the organisation's registration number and a receipt for tax purposes


-


Send a monthly impact update timed to arrive within 48 hours of each charge — donors are most receptive when a payment is fresh


-


Set up automatic failed-payment notifications so the fundraising team can reach out within 24 hours of a decline


-


Prompt donors to update card details before expiry — most platforms surface expiry data in the dashboard


Failed payments are the leading cause of involuntary churn in subscription and recurring donation models. A proactive dunning process — automated retries followed by a personal outreach — recovers a meaningful share of lapsed donors.


For nonprofits using invoice-based donations from institutional supporters,[HitPay's invoice payment tools](https://hitpayapp.com/blog/invoice-payment) offer a separate workflow suited to B2B and corporate donor relationships.


## What does a working recurring donation setup actually look like?


A children's literacy charity in Bonifacio Global City (BGC), Manila, runs a monthly giving programme that uses GCash recurring and ShopeePay recurring, with a monthly payment link for card donors. Donors choose their amount — ₱250, ₱500, or ₱1,000 — at sign-up. The link is shared via Facebook and embedded on the charity's website. The team receives automatic payouts each business day, reconciles against donor records monthly, and issues BIR-compliant receipts through the platform.


A similar model works in Tanjong Pagar, Singapore, where a community welfare organisation accepts PayNow and Mastercard recurring donations from corporate employee giving programmes — with payouts settling in SGD the next business day.


The infrastructure is the same across markets. The payment methods and currency differ.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### How do I set up recurring monthly donations for my nonprofit in Singapore?


Register with a MAS-licensed payment platform, submit charity documentation (registration certificate, financial statements, authorised signatory details), and create a recurring billing link once approved. HitPay supports recurring billing in Singapore with PayNow and card-on-file options, and payouts settle in SGD the next business day. Approval typically takes 1–3 business days after document submission is complete.


### What payment methods can Malaysian charities use to collect recurring donations?


Malaysian charities can collect recurring donations via Visa and Mastercard card-on-file (best for fully automated monthly charges), FPX bank transfer, Touch 'n Go e-wallet, and DuitNow QR. Card-on-file is the most reliable for automated recurring cycles as it requires no donor action after the initial sign-up. DuitNow QR and FPX are better suited to one-time or manually triggered donation flows.


### Can a Philippine nonprofit accept recurring GCash donations online?


Yes. With HitPay, donors in the Philippines authorise GCash once, and the monthly gift is collected automatically (2.9% per donation; payouts T+1). If you use HitPay's recurring billing software, its 0.2% fee also applies. HitPay supports GCash and ShopeePay recurring, for Philippine-registered organisations and for organisations outside the Philippines; cards by monthly payment link. Nonprofits must be registered with the SEC and compliant with BSP guidelines before a payment platform will activate recurring billing.


### Is there a monthly fee to use HitPay for nonprofit donation collection?


HitPay charges no monthly fees and no setup fees. Nonprofits pay only a per-transaction fee on each donation received. There are no minimum volume requirements. Full pricing details are available at hitpayapp.com/pricing.


### HitPay vs Stripe — which is better for a nonprofit collecting donations in Southeast Asia?


HitPay is purpose-built for Southeast Asian markets and supports local payment methods including PayNow, DuitNow QR, GCash, Maya, Touch 'n Go, and FPX — alongside card payments — with no monthly fees and next business day domestic payouts. Stripe supports cards and some regional wallets but requires more developer configuration for local e-wallet acceptance and is better suited to tech-forward teams with engineering resources. For a nonprofit in Singapore, Malaysia, or the Philippines that needs local payment method coverage without technical overhead, HitPay is the more operationally practical choice.


### How long does it take for a charity to get approved on a payment platform?


Approval timelines depend on the completeness of documentation submitted. HitPay's standard approval takes 1–3 business days for complete applications. Charities and religious organisations are classified as restricted business types and may require additional document review before the account is fully activated for live transactions. Submitting all required documents — registration certificate, financial statements, and authorised signatory details — at the time of application minimises delays.
